Built for your rack, barbell & bench

Legs. Push. Pull.
5 days. 60 minutes.

Your 3-day split, run on a rolling 5-day week — so every muscle gets hit twice every 8–9 days without ever training the same thing back-to-back. Core and a 10-minute cardio finisher are baked into every session, not bolted on if there's time.

5×days / week
60minutes flat
6workouts A / B
10 mincardio daily

How every hour is spent

Same clock every day. If a lift runs long, trim the last accessory — never the finisher. That's how the hour stays an hour.

0–5Warm-up
5–45 · Lifting1 big lift + 3 accessories · rest 60–120 sec
45–50Core block
50–60 · CardioFinisher — see each day
Warm-up (same daily, 5 min): 1 min easy walk / march in place, then 2 rounds of 8 bodyweight squats or bench push-ups (by day), 8 band pull-aparts, 6 walking lunges or dead bugs. Then 2 light ramp sets of the day's first lift. In summer, get the fan on and the door cracked before the warm-up, not after set two.

The rolling week

Don't restart the split on Mondays. Just pick up where you left off — Legs → Push → Pull → repeat. Weekends off.

Know the shapes before you load them

Every exercise in this plan is one of six shapes. If a position below doesn't match what you're doing, fix the shape first — then add weight.

The six workouts

Tap a day. Each one opens with a picture of its main lift and the three positions to hit. A = heavier, lower reps. B = same muscles, different angles and higher reps — so joints don't get hammered by the identical session twice in a row.

Legs A — Squat day

Quads first, heavy. The week’s anchor leg session.

Day warm-up add-on: 2 × 8 goblet squats with your lightest kettlebell before barbell ramp sets.
1 · SetBar on traps, brace hard, safeties one hole below depth2 · BottomSit between your heels to below parallel, knees tracking out3 · DrivePush the floor away — chest and hips rise together
ExerciseSets × RepsRest
1. Barbell Back SquatRack, safeties one hole below depth. Brace, sit between your heels, drive the floor away.4 × 5–62 min
2. Barbell Romanian DeadliftSoft knees, hinge and slide the bar down your thighs until hamstrings pull tight.3 × 890 sec
3. DB Bulgarian Split SquatRear foot on the bench. Most of your weight on the front leg; torso tall.3 × 8 / leg60 sec
4. Standing Calf RaiseBarbell on back or dumbbells in hand, heels off a bumper plate. Full stretch, 1-sec pause on top.3 × 12–1545 sec

Core · 5 min

Ab wheel 2 × 8–12 (from knees is fine) + dead bug 2 × 8 / side, back-to-back, minimal rest.

Cardio · 10 min EMOM

Kettlebell swing: 12 hard swings at the top of every minute × 10. Rest is whatever’s left of the minute. Hinge, don’t squat it.

Push A — Bench day

Chest, shoulders, triceps. Heavy horizontal pressing.

Day warm-up add-on: 15 band pull-aparts + 10 push-ups before bench ramp sets. Set the rack safeties just above chest height — you train solo.
1 · SetBlades pinched into the bench, feet planted, unrack over your chest2 · TouchLower under control to mid-chest, elbows tucked3 · PressDrive up and slightly back until your arms lock out
ExerciseSets × RepsRest
1. Barbell Bench PressFeet planted, shoulder blades pinched into the bench, bar to mid-chest.4 × 5–62 min
2. Incline DB PressBench at ~30°. Dumbbells let each side work on its own — no hiding a weak side.3 × 8–1090 sec
3. DB Lateral RaiseLight. Lead with elbows, stop at shoulder height. Superset with #4 to save time.3 × 12–15—
4. Band Triceps PushdownBand over the rack pull-up bar. Elbows pinned, full lockout.3 × 12–1560 sec*

* Rest after the pair, not between 3 and 4.

Core · 5 min

Decline sit-up on bench 2 × 12 (slow down-phase) + front plank 2 × 40 sec.

Cardio · 10 min intervals

30 / 30 × 10: 30 sec fast walk-out / jog in place or driveway shuttle, 30 sec easy. No kit needed, heart rate up without beating up your legs.

Pull A — Deadlift day

Posterior chain, lats and biceps. The heaviest pull of the cycle.

Day warm-up add-on: 2 × 6 light kettlebell deadlifts + 5 scap pull-ups (hang and shrug) before deadlift ramp sets.
1 · SetBar over mid-foot, flat back, lats tight like you're bending the bar2 · PullPush the floor away — the bar slides up your shins and thighs3 · StandHips through, glutes squeezed, then set it down and reset the next rep
ExerciseSets × RepsRest
1. Barbell DeadliftBar over mid-foot, lats tight like you’re bending the bar around your shins. Reset every rep — no bouncing bumpers.4 × 52 min
2. Pull-UpRack bar. Full hang to chin over. Short? Loop a band under a knee for assistance and chase unassisted reps over weeks.4 × AMRAP −190 sec
3. Barbell Bent-Over RowHinge to ~45°, row to lower ribs, no bouncing. Lighter than you think.3 × 890 sec
4. DB Hammer CurlNeutral grip, elbows still. Superset with band face pulls if you want the rear delts too.3 × 10–1260 sec

Core · 5 min

Hanging knee raise from the pull-up bar 3 × 10 — knees to chest, no swinging. Grip work comes free.

Cardio · 10 min carry medley

Repeat for 10 min: 40 m farmer’s carry (heaviest DBs/KBs) + 10 KB swings. Rest 30 sec between rounds.

Legs B — Hinge & single-leg day

Glutes, hamstrings and balance. Less barbell load, more burn.

Day warm-up add-on: 2 × 8 glute bridges + 6 reverse lunges per side, bodyweight only.
1 · SetBar resting on front delts, elbows high, torso tall2 · BottomSit straight down, knees forward, heels stay down3 · DrivePush through the whole foot and keep the elbows up
ExerciseSets × RepsRest
1. Barbell Front SquatBar in the rack position (or crossed-arm), elbows high, torso upright. Lighter than Legs A — that’s the point.4 × 62 min
2. Barbell Hip ThrustUpper back on the bench, bar over hips (pad it with a towel). Chin tucked, ribs down, squeeze at the top.3 × 8–1090 sec
3. DB Reverse LungeStep back, front shin fairly vertical. Easier on knees than walking lunges in a tight garage bay.3 × 8 / leg60 sec
4. Single-Leg KB Romanian DeadliftLight kettlebell, opposite hand. Slow — this is hamstrings plus ankle / hip stability.2 × 10 / leg45 sec

Core · 5 min

Side plank 2 × 35 sec / side + Pallof press (band on rack) 2 × 10 / side.

Cardio · 10 min EMOM

Alternate minutes × 10: Minute A: 10 goblet squats · Minute B: 8 KB deadlifts. Steady, nasal breathing if you can.

Push B — Overhead day

Shoulders lead this time, bench becomes the accessory.

Day warm-up add-on: 12 band external rotations / side + 8 TRX push-ups before pressing.
1 · SetBar at collarbone, glutes squeezed, ribs down2 · PressTuck your head back and press in a straight line3 · Lock outBiceps by your ears, head through — no leaning back
ExerciseSets × RepsRest
1. Barbell Overhead PressStanding, in the rack. Glutes squeezed, bar path straight — move your head, not your lower back.4 × 62 min
2. Incline Barbell Bench PressBench at ~30° inside the rack, safeties set. Touch high on the chest.3 × 890 sec
3. Landmine PressBar in your landmine attachment, half-kneeling. Garage-gym gold: shoulder-friendly and it doubles as core work.3 × 10 / side60 sec
4. TRX Triceps Extension / Push-UpStraps from the ceiling mount. Body angle sets the difficulty — walk your feet back to make it harder.3 × 10–1260 sec

Core · 5 min

Pallof press 2 × 10 / side + dead bug 2 × 8 / side. Anti-rotation is what protects your back on overhead days.

Cardio · 10 min ladder

DB push press ladder: 2-4-6-8-10-8-6-4-2 reps, 20 sec rest between rungs. Light dumbbells — speed, not load. Fill any leftover time with an easy walk.

Pull B — Row volume day

No heavy deadlift. Rows, TRX and arms — back thickness without the fatigue bill.

Day warm-up add-on: 2 × 10 TRX rows at an easy angle + 10 band pull-aparts.
1 · SetHinge to about 45°, chest tall, grip low on the bar2 · RowPull to your stomach, elbows tracking back, no bouncing3 · StretchLower slowly to straight arms before the next rep
ExerciseSets × RepsRest
1. Landmine T-Bar RowBar in the landmine, V-handle or towel through your hands, chest tall, row to your stomach. The best row your setup allows.4 × 8–1090 sec
2. Chin-Up or TRX RowChin-ups if you’ve got 6+ clean reps; otherwise TRX rows with feet walked forward. Full stretch at the bottom.3 × 8–1290 sec
3. One-Arm DB RowFree hand and knee on the bench. Row to your hip pocket, not your armpit.3 × 10 / side60 sec
4. DB Curl + Band Face PullSuperset: 10 curls, then 15 face pulls (band at eye height on the rack). Posture insurance for desk work.3 × 10 + 1560 sec*

* Rest after the pair.

Core · 5 min

Ab wheel 2 × 10 + KB Russian twist 2 × 10 / side (light — rotate your ribs, don’t yank with your arms).

Cardio · 10 min EMOM

KB swing EMOM again, +2 reps: 14 swings / minute × 10. If Legs A’s 12 felt easy, this is where you find out.

How to progress (and not stall)

Add load the simple way

  • Main lifts (4 × 5–6): when you hit the top of the range on all sets with 1–2 reps in reserve, add 5 lb upper body / 10 lb lower body next time.
  • Accessories: beat last week by reps first. When you’re at the top of the range everywhere, go up one dumbbell / plate.
  • Effort: most sets at RPE 7–9 — hard, but never a grind that wrecks your form. Last set can touch RPE 9.
  • Every 6th week: deload — same workouts, ~60% of the load, finishers at easy pace. You’ll come back stronger, not just less tired.

Keep it to an hour

  • Set a visible timer at minute 0. Lifting ends at :45 whether you’re “done” or not.
  • Supersets are already written in where they save real time (Push A #3–4, Pull B #4).
  • Load the bar for the next exercise during the previous rest period.
  • Short on time one day? Do the main lift + core + finisher only. That 30-minute version beats skipping.

Scottsdale garage rules

An Arizona garage in summer is a sauna with a squat rack in it. Train early morning when you can, run a fan across the platform, keep water in the gym (not inside the house), and on 105°+ days cut finisher intensity in half — steady carries and walks count. Heat exhaustion is not progressive overload.

Solo-training safety

  • Safeties set on every squat and bench session — just below where the bar would need to stop.
  • Never bench to failure alone without safeties; leave 1 rep in the tank.
  • Collars on for squats / deadlifts, off for bench if you ever need to dump a side (with safeties, you won’t).
Program built only from your kit: rack + pull-up bar, barbell + bumper plates, adjustable bench, dumbbell rack, kettlebells, landmine, TRX, bands and ab wheel. No cable machine, treadmill or bike assumed — every finisher uses what you own or your driveway. The illustrations show the position each main lift should pass through; they're guides, not form coaching — if a movement hurts (sharp pain, not effort), swap it and get it checked.
